state.title: bug: gc hook --claim work query can consume the whole claim window on a serialized shared dolt server while a direct bd claim completes in seconds
state.body:
## Title

```
bug: hook --claim work query can consume the whole claim window on a serialized shared dolt server while a direct bd claim completes in seconds
```

## Summary

On a multi-rig city backed by a single shared (serialized) Dolt sql-server, `gc hook --claim --json`
repeatedly exceeds ~110 s and appears hung to the agent, while the same claim performed directly
(`bd ready` + `bd update <id> --claim`) completes in ~2 s and a bare `gc hook <agent> --json` returns
in ~15 s. The claim window is sized from the work-query timeout plus the mutation timeout
(`hookClaimWindowDefault = hookWorkQueryTimeout + hookClaimMutationTimeout`, `cmd_hook_claim.go`),
and the work query is bounded at 150 s (`cmd_hook.go`, raised 60→150 s on 2026-08-14 because the
~6-leg sequential probe was already exceeding 30 s under load). The design therefore *schedules*
multi-minute claim latencies on exactly the deployments (one Dolt server serving every rig's store)
the docs recommend, and the agent-visible behavior is indistinguishable from a hang.

## Environment

- macOS 27.0 (arm64), gc 1.4.1 via Homebrew (`beads` pinned 1.2.2, in-process NativeDoltStore active)
- One managed Dolt sql-server (127.0.0.1) serving **10 rig databases + hq** for a 10-rig city
- `probe_concurrency` unset → default 8 concurrent bd subprocess probes
  (`internal/config/config.go`: "bd serializes on a shared dolt sql-server, so unbounded
  parallelism causes contention" — the config comment itself names this contention mode)
- Contention source: pool scale-check + work-query probes from concurrent worker sessions and the
  reconciler, all hitting the same serialized server

## Reproduction

1. Run a multi-rig city (≥4 rigs, ~10 databases) on one shared Dolt server; have several workers
   and the reconciler issuing probes concurrently.
2. From a worker session run `gc hook <agent> --claim --json`.
3. Under load the command runs >110 s (observed repeatedly in production use, 2026-09-15); with the
   city idle the same command returns in ~11 s, and the non-claim hook returns in ~7-15 s.
4. Independently: `bd ready --json` (~1.4 s) and `bd update <id> --claim` (~2 s) complete against
   the same contended server.

Smallest observable differential (same server, same minute, idle city):

| Command | Wall time |
|---|---|
| `gc hook <agent> --json` (no claim) | ~7 s |
| `gc hook <agent> --claim --json` | ~11 s (loaded: >110 s) |
| `bd ready --json` | ~1.4 s |
| `bd update <id> --claim` | ~2 s |

## Expected behavior

An atomic claim should not be starved by the discovery probe. The claim CAS is a cheap single-store
mutation (`hookClaimMutationTimeout = 10 s`, correctly bounded); the expensive part is the
*federated routed-work query* in front of it, which re-runs the multi-leg probe (config comment:
"~6 sequential bd/store round-trips") on every claim attempt, serially competing with the very
contention it generates. Expected: claim latency stays O(mutation), discovery cost is capped or
cached, and a claim that finds work quickly claims it quickly.

## Actual behavior

- The work query legitimately runs up to 150 s (`hookWorkQueryTimeout`), and the claim window is
  derived from it (160 s total), so >110 s claim attempts are *by design* rather than a failure
  signal — but from the agent's seat they are indistinguishable from a hung process, and the
  documented work loop ("run `gc hook --claim`, repeat after closing") serializes this cost into
  every work item.
- Under concurrent probe load the serialized Dolt server makes each probe leg slower, so the
  system is at its worst exactly when the most workers are trying to claim: probe concurrency 8
  amplifies load; the raised 150 s bound converts the amplification into multi-minute waits.
- gascity's own history anticipates this shape: `cmd_hook.go` records 850+ `session.work_query_failed`
  events at the old 60 s bound ("every hook starved while `gc ready` run standalone returned the
  routed rows"). The bound was raised rather than the round-trip count reduced ("the real cure
  remains ga-4qdfn (fewer round-trips, faster reader)").

## Evidence

- Timing table above (production Mac, gc 1.4.1; >110 s observations from loaded city 2026-09-15)
- `cmd_hook.go:907-926` — `hookWorkQueryTimeout = 150s` with the 850+-events starvation history in
  the comment
- `cmd_hook_claim.go:58-85` — `hookClaimMutationTimeout = 10s`,
  `hookClaimWindowDefault = hookWorkQueryTimeout + hookClaimMutationTimeout`, comment: "a loaded
  multi-rig city's federated probe legitimately runs tens of seconds"
- `internal/config/config.go:2602-2607` — `probe_concurrency` default 8, comment naming bd
  serialization on a shared dolt sql-server as the contention cause
- `internal/doltpool/pool.go` — pooled *sql.DB handles with ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout 30 s exist for
  gc's Go-native paths; note `internal/api/convoy_sql.go:buildDoltDSN` sets dial `Timeout` but no
  `ReadTimeout`/`WriteTimeout`, so that path can hold a dead connection until TCP gives up
  (related, possibly distinct issue — flagging for triage)
- Transient CLOSE_WAIT connections on the client side observed during loaded windows (consistent
  with a response the client never reads back; not present at idle) — `lsof -nP -iTCP:<dolt-port>`

## Additional context

- Workers on this city now bypass `gc hook --claim` entirely (`bd ready` + `bd update --claim`)
  because the direct path is ~50× faster; this routes around atomic-claim bookkeeping, which is
  the integration smell that made us file.
- Possibly related known issue (same command, different failure mode): idle workers re-claim beads
  parked blocked-on-human, churning park/reclaim loops. Both suggest the claim protocol's
  discovery stage needs the rework ga-4qdfn anticipated.
- Suggested directions (maintainer's call): split claim into discover-fast (bounded, cheap,
  cache-friendly) + claim-fast (CAS, already bounded); let `--claim` accept a hint bead id;
  reduce probe round-trips per the existing ga-4qdfn note; expose claim-window progress so a
  multi-minute wait is distinguishable from a hang.

## Mitigation we ship locally (for the runbook PR, not upstream)

Documented in the cityworker work loop (`city/agents/cityworker/prompt.template.md`, "Work Loop →
KNOWN ISSUE 2026-09-15"): if `gc hook --claim` exceeds 60 s, fall back to
`gc bd ready --unassigned --sort oldest -t task --json` + `gc bd update <id> --claim`, verifying
assignee afterwards (command shape verified against gc 1.4.1: `--sort oldest` is the valid value,
not `created_at`). Race window acknowledged and accepted at city scale; explicit drain/no_work
results are still honored, timeouts are never treated as empty queues, and `gc hook --claim`
remains the primary path.
